title: [Audit] Memory leaks and memory-safety defects in core nntrainer code (83 items)

events.body_markdown:
# Issue Description

This is a consolidated memory-safety audit (leaks, use-after-free, double free, out-of-bounds, uninitialized reads, object-lifetime bugs) of the **core** NNTrainer code: `nntrainer/` and `api/`. `test/`, `Applications/`, plugins and model implementations were out of scope (they were only read to trace callers). Each item is an independent defect with location, evidence, trigger and a suggested fix so that a developer can pick it up on its own. Please tick the box or link the PR when an item is fixed; items that turn out to be intentional can be struck through with a short note.

* Audit base: `a7ea056e` on `main` (2026-09-10). Line numbers refer to that commit; the first link of every item is a permalink.
* Excluded because already reported / in flight: #3783 (`incremental_inference` output buffer leak), #3510 (`Tensor::activate` mmap leak), #2993 (`NNTR_THROW_IF` `c_str()` lifetime), #4333 (causal mask), #4300 (`RunLayerContext::validate()` `inputs[0]` OOB, in-place aliasing asserts), #4302 (`unpack_q4_0x8_transpose16` `K % 256` assert).
* Severity: **H** = memory corruption / UAF / double free / unbounded leak reachable from a public API or a supported configuration. **M** = corruption or leak that needs a specific configuration. **L** = latent (needs a path that no in-tree caller uses today) or a bounded leak.
* Note on `assert`: nothing in `meson.build` / packaging defines `NDEBUG`, so `assert()`/`KAI_ASSERT` abort in release builds too. Items marked "assert" crash instead of corrupting memory today, but become silent OOB the moment `-DNDEBUG` is added.

Expected Result
============
No item below should be reproducible (ASan/UBSan clean) after the fixes.

How to Reproduce
===============
Each item carries its own trigger. Most can be reproduced with a small gtest plus `meson -Db_sanitize=address,undefined`.

Further Information
===============

## A. Tensor memory management / FSU (`nntrainer/tensor/`)

- [ ] **A1 (H, lifetime/UAF)** [`cache_pool.cpp:229-230`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cache_pool.cpp#L229-L230), `cache_pool.cpp:308-313`, `cache_elem.cpp:49-57` — `CachePool` keeps stale `CacheElem`s across `deallocate()` / re-`finalize()` / re-`allocate()`. `getMemory()` does `elems.emplace(id, …)`, which is a no-op when the id already exists, and `clear()`/`deallocate()` never clear `elems`/`exec_ids`. After a second `finalize()+allocate()` (ids are reused), each tensor receives a new `MemoryData` M2, but `validate(id)` → `elems[id]->swapIn()` sets the address on the *old* M1 with the old offset/length (and, in INFERENCE mode, the old freed `memory_ptr`). `getData()` then returns `nullptr + offset` (segfault), or `SwapDevice::getBuffer` `memcpy`s into the freed `memory_ptr` (heap UAF write). Trigger: `fsu=true` model with two allocation cycles (`train()` twice, `train()` then `inference()`, `inference()` twice — see `neuralnet.cpp:1646-1648,1687,1699`). Fix: clear `elems`, `exec_ids`, `actives` in `CachePool::clear()`/`deallocate()` (or use `insert_or_assign`). — PR https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/4380 (in progress)
- [ ] **A2 (M, fd leak/lifetime)** [`cache_pool.cpp:163-176`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cache_pool.cpp#L163-L176), `swap_device.cpp:77-107,153-164`, `cache_loader.cpp:195-207` — In INFERENCE FSU mode `SwapDevice::getBuffer` returns the pool's `memory_ptr` without recording it in `mapped`, so `putBuffer(memory_ptr)` throws "Couldn't find buffer". `CachePool::deallocate()` calls `invalidate(id)` → `swapOut()` → `putBuffer()` for every element still active, throws, and never reaches `swap_device->finish()`: the weight-file fd is leaked and `isAllocated()` stays true (the pool can never be re-finalized). Elements stay active because `CacheLoader::inActive(order)` calls `pool->inActive(id)` with a *tensor id* where `CachePool::inActive(unsigned order)` indexes `exec_ids[order]`. Reproduces on every destruction of an FSU inference model (`integration_test_fsu.cpp`). Fix: skip `swapOut()` in INFERENCE mode (just clear addresses), and pass `order` (not `id`) in `CacheLoader::inActive`.
- [ ] **A3 (M, OOB write)** [`swap_device.cpp:79-100`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/swap_device.cpp#L79-L100), `neuralnet.cpp:975-984`, `memory_pool.cpp:209-216` — For quantized weights with qparams `NeuralNetwork::load` registers `size = getMemoryBytes() + sizeof(uint16_t)` (the qscheme header) as the FSU record length, but `MemoryPool::allocateFSU` allocates exactly `getMemoryBytes()` per weight. `getBuffer` then `memcpy(memory_ptr, buf, len_offset.second)` copies 2 bytes past the buffer (a real overflow whenever `getMemoryBytes()` is a page multiple) and the data is shifted by the 2-byte header (wrong weights in all cases). Trigger: `fsu=true` inference with QINT8/QINT4/UINT*/BCQ/Q4_K weights. Fix: copy only `getMemoryBytes()` bytes after the header and bound-check `len` against the buffer size.
- [ ] **A4 (L, unbounded growth)** [`tensor_pool.h:83-86`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/tensor_pool.h#L83-L86), `tensor_pool.cpp:128-135,191` — `TensorPool::reinitialize()` clears only `name_map` and swaps in a new `MemoryPool`; the old `RequestSpec`s (with valid exec orders) stay in `pool`, so every later `finalize()` re-plans and `allocate()` re-binds them. Activation memory doubles on each `NeuralNetwork::reinitialize()`. It also replaces an FSU `CachePool` by a plain `MemoryPool` while `cache_loader` still holds the old pool. Fix: clear `pool` after `deallocate()`, and recreate the CachePool/CacheLoader pair when FSU is on.
- [ ] **A5 (L, leak)** [`swap_device.cpp:130-141`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/swap_device.cpp#L130-L141) — non-`USE_MMAP` `getBuffer`: `ptr = calloc(1, size)` is leaked when the following `lseek`/`read` `NNTR_THROW_IF` fires (not yet inserted into `allocated`). Fix: hold `ptr` in `unique_ptr<void, decltype(&free)>` until registered.
- [ ] **A6 (L, mismatched free)** [`swap_device.cpp:240-247`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/swap_device.cpp#L240-L247) — `finish()` (TRAIN, `USE_MMAP`) calls `free(ptr)` on keys of `mapped`, which are `mmap` base + page diff (`swap_device.cpp:118-121`). Reached whenever mappings survive to `finish()` (an earlier `putBuffer` write failure, or `setFsuWeightPath()` on an active pool). Fix: `munmap(std::get<0>(info), std::get<1>(info))`.
- [ ] **A7 (L, handle leak)** [`mman_windows.cpp:95-118`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/utils/mman_windows.cpp#L95-L118) — Windows `mmap()` shim: when `MapViewOfFile(Ex)` fails the `CreateFileMapping` HANDLE is never closed (`return MAP_FAILED` before `CloseHandle`). The `MAP_FIXED` branch condition is also inverted. Fix: `CloseHandle(file_mapping)` on the failure path.

## B. Tensor classes (`nntrainer/tensor/*_tensor.cpp`, `tensor.cpp`)

- [ ] **B1 (M, OOB)** [`int4_tensor.cpp:143-145`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/int4_tensor.cpp#L143-L145) vs `int4_tensor.cpp:556-559` — `Int4QTensor` has two incompatible scale layouts: `allocate()`, the vector ctor, `copy(const void*)`, `operator==` and `print()` use 4-byte (`float`) scales, while `getMemoryBytes()`, `read()`, `save()` and `FloatTensor::dotQInteger` use 2-byte (`uint16_t`) scales. Pool-backed QINT4 weights get exactly `getMemoryBytes()` bytes (`tensor_pool.cpp:191`), so `Tensor::copy()`/`copyData()` into them writes `2*scale_size()` bytes past the block (corrupting the adjacent weight), and `clone()`/`==`/`print()` read past it. Fix: settle on one scale format (FP16, matching the file format and kernels) in every member.
- [ ] **B2 (M, OOB read)** [`uint4_tensor.cpp:629-636`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/uint4_tensor.cpp#L629-L636) — `Uint4QTensor::copy(const void*)` locates zero points at `buf + size() + 4*scale_size()` although the packed data occupies `(size()+1)/2` bytes (line 629 uses the right value). The `memcpy` reads ~`size()/2` bytes past the source and copies garbage zero points. Triggered by `Tensor::clone()`/`copy()` of any UINT4 tensor. `Q4_K_Tensor` inherits this `copy()` and copies only half of its packed bytes. Fix: `((uint8_t*)buf) + (size()+1)/2 + scale_size()*sizeof(float)`; give `Q4_K_Tensor` its own `copy()`. — PR https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/4379 (in progress)
- [ ] **B3 (L, OOB read)** [`char_tensor.cpp:552-556`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/char_tensor.cpp#L552-L556), `short_tensor.cpp:453-457`, `int4_tensor.cpp:542-546`, `uint4_tensor.cpp:571-580`, `uint_tensor.cpp:537-546` — `print()` indexes the scale (and zero-point) array with `len = size()` (`q_scales[len-1]`) although it has only `scale_size()` entries. Any per-channel quantized tensor with `scale_size() > 50` and more than one row reads far past the array. Fix: use `scale_size()` like `BCQTensor::printScales`.
- [ ] **B4 (M, double munmap / UAF)** [`tensor.cpp:315-319`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/tensor.cpp#L315-L319), `tensor.h:452-456,468,480` — `mapped_ptr` is an owning resource (`~Tensor` → `deactivate()` → `munmap`), but the copy ctor / copy assignment duplicate it and the defaulted move ops leave the source with `is_virtual==true`, `mapped_ptr!=nullptr`, `itensor_==nullptr`. Any temporary copy of an activated virtual tensor (`getSharedDataTensor`, `getBatchSlice`, `Tensor tmp = *this` in `normalization_i`, `std::vector<Tensor>` growth) unmaps the region while the original still uses it, and the original unmaps it again on destruction; a moved-from tensor dereferences a null `itensor_` in `deactivate()`. `deactivate()` can also throw from the `noexcept` destructor. Fix: own the mapping through RAII (e.g. a `MemoryData` deleter) and write proper copy/move semantics.
- [ ] **B5 (M, OOB read)** [`tensor_base.cpp:216-244`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/tensor_base.cpp#L216-L244), `embedding.cpp:94-111` — `getSharedDataTensor` checks only the format and overwrites the view's `dim` (and thus data type) with the requested one, and its element offset is added as a *byte* offset by the packed types' `getData()` (`int4_tensor.cpp:161-167`, `uint4_tensor.cpp:164-170`, `q4_0_tensor.cpp:66-72`). `EmbeddingLayer::forwarding` builds `out_tensor_dim` with the activation type (FP32) on a QINT8/QINT4 weight, so `copyData` reads `4*out_dim` bytes from a region holding `out_dim` / `out_dim/2` bytes, at a doubled offset for QINT4 — past the weight allocation for roughly the upper half of the vocabulary. Trigger: `model_tensor_type=QINT8-FP32` / `QINT4-FP32` with `EmbeddingLayer`. Fix: throw on data-type mismatch in `getSharedDataTensor`, convert offsets to bytes per type, and dequantize explicitly in `EmbeddingLayer`.
- [ ] **B6 (M, heap overflow)** [`char_tensor.cpp:425-446`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/char_tensor.cpp#L425-L446), `short_tensor.cpp:326-347`, `int4_tensor.cpp:357-401`, `uint4_tensor.cpp:385-429`, `uint_tensor.cpp:391-441` — `read()` first overwrites the `qscheme` member with the value from the file and then reads `getMemoryBytes()` (computed from the *new* scheme) into the buffer allocated for the *old* scheme. A standalone `PER_TENSOR_AFFINE` tensor reading a `PER_CHANNEL_AFFINE` file (or a corrupted `.bin`) overruns the buffer by `4*(width-1)` bytes. Fix: validate the on-file scheme against the allocated scheme/size before `checkedRead`.
- [ ] **B7 (L, uninitialized read)** [`half_tensor.cpp:638-648`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/half_tensor.cpp#L638-L648), `half_tensor.cpp:66`, `sqrt_layer.cpp:34-38` — `HalfTensor::inv_sqrt(out)` ignores `*this` and runs the in-place kernel on `out` (`FloatTensor::inv_sqrt` maps `this → out`), so `SQRTLayer::calcDerivative` with FP16 activations computes `1/sqrt(stale derivative buffer)`; `HalfTensor::allocate` uses `new _FP16[n]` without value-initialization (unlike `FloatTensor`), so the read is of never-written memory. Fix: copy `*this` into `out` first; value-initialize in `HalfTensor::allocate` / `UIntTensor::allocate`.
- [ ] **B8 (L, lifetime)** [`tensor.cpp:358-402`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/tensor.cpp#L358-L402), `tensor.cpp:322-356` — `Tensor::operator=(const Tensor&)` has no `QS4CX` branch (leaves `itensor_` untouched while copying `is_virtual/fd/mapped_ptr`), and `Tensor(const std::unique_ptr<TensorBase>&)` has no `Q4_0/Q4_K/Q6_K/QS4CX` branch (leaves `itensor_` null). Fix: add the branches (or a shared clone helper) and throw in the final `else`.

## C. CPU backend (`nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/`)

- [ ] **C1 (H on the generic fallback backend, OOB read)** [`fallback/fallback.cpp:85-91`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/fallback/fallback.cpp#L85-L91) — `sgemv()` forwards `Y` where `X` is expected: `__fallback_sgemv(..., A, lda, Y, incX, beta, Y, incY)`. The kernel reads `Y[cj*incX]` for `cj < N` from the `M`-element output (OOB whenever `N > M`, e.g. any FC layer with input width > batch) and the result is garbage. Present since 41f83688; only compiled on targets that are neither ARM nor x86 (`cpu_backend.h:17-26`). (`fallback.cpp:291` `quantize_row_q8_K` specialization also does not match its primary template, i.e. this backend does not currently compile — CI never exercises it.) Fix: pass `X`.
- [ ] **C2 (L, latent OOB)** [`fallback/fallback_internal.cpp:140-154`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/fallback/fallback_internal.cpp#L140-L154), `:166-180` — `__fallback_scopy` (uint8/int8) and `__fallback_scopy_{u,}int8_to_float32` index `Y[idx*incX] = X[idx*incY]` (strides swapped). All current callers pass `1,1`; any strided call (also reached from x86 via `x86_compute_backend.cpp:133-143,214-222`) would read/write out of bounds. Fix: swap the strides.
- [ ] **C3 (H, OOB read/write, ARM fp16)** [`arm/hgemm/hgemm_transB.cpp:78-85`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/arm/hgemm/hgemm_transB.cpp#L78-L85) — `hgemm_transB_8x16` rounds the N remainder to a multiple of `GEMM_UNROLLING_8` (`(n_min/2 + 7) & ~7`, line 82), but `packing_transB16` (`hgemm_pack.cpp:417`) and `hgemm_kernel_8x16` (`hgemm_kernel_8x16.cpp:328`) consume 16 columns per step (the noTrans path at `hgemm_noTrans.cpp:887` correctly uses 16). For padded N > 1536 with N ≡ 16 (mod 32) — e.g. `HalfTensor::dot(x, W, false, true)` / MHA Q·Kᵀ with key length 1537..1552 — the block is 392: `packing_transB16` asserts `N % 16 == 0` (abort); under `NDEBUG` it reads 8 rows past the padded `B` and the kernel writes 8 floats past the last row of the `malloc`'d `C32`. Fix: use `GEMM_UNROLLING_16`. — PR https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/4373 (in progress)
- [ ] **C4 (H, OOB read/write, ARM fp32)** [`arm/matrix_transpose_neon/matrix_transpose_neon.cpp:58-66`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/arm/matrix_transpose_neon/matrix_transpose_neon.cpp#L58-L66), `:115-123,145,173-181` — `transpose_neon<float>` handles remainders by re-transposing the last full 4x4 tile at `(N_blocks*4 - (4 - N_left))`; for `N < 4` or `M < 4` this wraps in `unsigned int` and loads/stores gigabytes away. Reached from `FloatTensor::transpose("0:2:1")` (`float_tensor.cpp:1305`) for any NCHW tensor with height < 4 or width < 4 on the ARM backend (e.g. `tflite_opnode.cpp:205` FC weight transpose with 1..3 units, `layer_devel.h:412/432` QS4CX save). The `__fp16` overload handles small sizes correctly. Fix: scalar tail for `M<4 || N<4`.
- [ ] **C5 (M, assert abort)** [`arm/hgemm/hgemm_noTrans.cpp:176-186`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/arm/hgemm/hgemm_noTrans.cpp#L176-L186), `:356-393`, `hgemm_pack.cpp:28` — `hgemm_small` → `hgemm_noTrans_1x8/1x4` calls `packing_A1(m2_min ∈ {1,2,3}, …)` whose `assert(m % 4 == 0)` always fails. Trigger: `hgemm` with `M ∈ {1,2,3,5,6,7}`, `N ∈ {4,8,12}`, `K = 8` (e.g. a (3x8)·(8x8) fp16 dot). Memory-safe under `NDEBUG`. Fix: relax the assert (the loop supports any m) or route to `hgemm_noTrans_fallback`. Latent copies of the C3 rounding bug also exist in unreachable paths: `hgemm_noTrans.cpp:819,613,405`, and `hgemm_transB` K-blocking when `K % 16 != 0`. — PR https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/4375 (in progress)
- [ ] **C6 (H, unbounded OOB write, ARM with `thread-backend=bstp|mixed`)** [`ggml_interface/ggml_interface_bs_threadpool.cpp:90-104`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/ggml_interface/ggml_interface_bs_threadpool.cpp#L90-L104), `:44-58,107-123`, `ggml_interface_mixed.cpp` same lines, `ggml_interface_omp.cpp:225-277` (multi-weight entry points); kernels `nntr_ggml_impl/nntr_ggml_impl_neon.cpp:534-536,568,671-673`, `nntr_ggml_impl_sve.cpp:96-99,366-367,502-504,792-793,929-931,2060-2063` — The upstream-derived asm GEMM/GEMV kernels loop `do { store tile; nc -= 4; } while (nc != 0)`. The thread-split callers compute `[ceil4(i*N/t), ceil4((i+1)*N/t))` with no `start >= end` guard (upstream ggml has `if (src0_start >= src0_end) return;`), so whenever `N/thread_num < 4` (e.g. `N=96` with 32 compute threads, `N=32` with 12) a thread gets `nc == 0`: the asm writes one tile, `nc` wraps to `0xFFFF…FFFC`, and it keeps streaming stores across `C` and loads across `B` until it faults. Affects NEON `nntr_gemm_q4_0_4x8_q8_0` (asm only, every AArch64 build) and the SVE GEMVs; the default `omp` backend's single-weight paths use `min(chunk, N)` chunking and are safe. Fix: `if (M_step_start >= M_step_end) return;` in every split caller, plus `if (nc <= 0) return;` in the kernels. — PR https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/4377 (in progress)
- [ ] **C7 (M, latent OOB)** [`ggml_interface/nntr_ggml_impl/nntr_ggml_impl_sve.cpp:539-599`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/ggml_interface/nntr_ggml_impl/nntr_ggml_impl_sve.cpp#L539-L599), `:792-824,2010-2062` — The SVE q4_0 8x8 asm uses unpredicated full-VL `ld1b`/`st1w` with fixed 144-byte / 32-byte strides; upstream guards it with `svcntb() == QK8_0` (256-bit VL) and the port dropped the check. On 512-bit SVE it reads 128 B past `B` and writes 8 floats past every result tile; on 128-bit cores (the `armv9.2-a` targets in `meson.build:189`) half of each output tile is left unwritten. `sve.cpp:1817` likewise hard-codes `vector_length` for the q6_K dot (all-false predicate → zero results on 128-bit cores). Not dispatched by `arm_compute_backend.cpp` today (only from the x86 table), hence latent. Fix: restore the `svcntb()` guard with a scalar fallback.
- [ ] **C8 (M, OOB read)** [`ggml_interface/ggml_interface_omp.cpp:712-729`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/ggml_interface/ggml_interface_omp.cpp#L712-L729), `:746-750`; same in `ggml_interface_bs_threadpool.cpp:756-783`, `ggml_interface_mixed.cpp:757-784`, `ggml_interface_fp16.cpp:336-376`; `q6_k_tensor.cpp:23,73` — `__ggml_gemm_q6_K` strides B rows by `sizeof(block_q6_K) * ceil(K/256)` while `Q6_K_Tensor` allocates `floor(K*N/256)` blocks and validates only `width % 256` (K is the height when `trans_in=false`). For `K % 256 != 0` (e.g. K=896, N=4864) the last rows are read hundreds of KB past the weight. Fix: reject `K % QK_K != 0` in the wrappers and validate the K dimension in `Q6_K_Tensor`/`Q4_K_Tensor`.
- [ ] **C9 (M, OOB write/read)** [`ggml_interface/ggml_interface.cpp:109-134`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/tensor/cpu_backend/ggml_interface/ggml_interface.cpp#L109-L134), `ggml_interface_omp.cpp:298-308` (+ all thread-split callers), `float_tensor.cpp:1046-1048,822-826`, `quantizer.cpp:275-304` — `nntr_repack_*` return `-1` without writing when `N % 4/8 != 0`, but the `__ggml_repack_*` wrappers and `GgmlQuantizer::quantize` ignore it. The GEMM/GEMV callers round `M_step_end` *up* to a multiple of 8 (x86) / 4 (ARM), so with such N the kernel writes up to 7 floats past every C row and reads a full extra row-group of B. Concretely reachable through the QINT4 CPU fallback in `FloatTensor::dotQInteger`: `Int4QTensor` has no dimension constraint and its `N*K/2` data bytes are interpreted as `0.5625*N*K` bytes of `block_q4_0` (unconditional ~6% over-read of the int4 buffer). Fix: propagate the repack return code, validate `N % NB_COLS == 0` at wrapper entry, remove or guard the QINT4→`gemm_q4_0` placeholder.

### Two further defects in `conv2d_transpose_layer.cpp`, found while fixing F1

Both were found while fixing item **F1** in PR https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/4347 — recording them here so nobody re-reports them. Neither is one of the 83 audited items.

---

**1. `col2im_transpose()` reads the column matrix with the row and column index swapped — OOB read. Fixed in #4347 together with F1.**

[`conv2d_transpose_layer.cpp:112`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/layers/conv2d_transpose_layer.cpp#L112)

```cpp
*val += col_matrix.getValue<float>(0, 0, out_i, out_j);
```

`calcDerivative` allocates the matrix as `calcCol2ImOutputDim(derivative.getDim(), filter_dim)`, i.e. `[in_channel*k_h*k_w] x [out_h*out_w]`, and fills it with `filter_kernel.dot(deriv_sub, result, true, false)`. It is never reshaped — unlike the matrix `im2col_transpose` fills, which *is* reshaped to the transposed layout. But `out_i` walks output positions and `out_j` walks `(c, r, s)`, so the two indices are the wrong way round. `getValue(b,c,h,w)` resolves to `h * width + w` with `width = out_h*out_w`, so the access runs off the end of the buffer.

Concretely, for a `1:1:3:3` input with `kernel_size=2,2` the last offset read is **243 in a 64-element buffer**; the outgoing derivative comes out as `[2 2 2 0 0 0 0 0 0]` instead of `[4 4 4 4 4 4 4 4 4]`. A 2-filter / 2-channel `1:2:1:1` case gives `[52 60]` instead of `[52 84]`. It is harmless only when the matrix happens to be square and the needed entries fall on the diagonal (e.g. a `1:1:1:1` input with a 3x3 kernel), which is why it is not visible in every shape.

Fix (in #4347): `col_matrix.getValue<float>(0, 0, out_j, out_i)`. Folded into the F1 PR because it is the same helper, the same loop and the same class of defect, and the F1 regression test for the backward path cannot pass without it.

---

**2. The `result` column matrix is shared across the batch loop — wrong results for `batch > 1`. NOT fixed in #4347; needs its own item.**

[`conv2d_transpose_layer.cpp:363-373`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/layers/conv2d_transpose_layer.cpp#L363-L373) (`forwarding`), `:485-500` and `:516-531` (`calcGradient`, both the threaded and the serial branch)

```cpp
Tensor result = Tensor(calcCol2ImOutputDim(out_dim, filter_dim));
result.setZero();                       // zeroed once, outside the loop
for (unsigned int b = s; b < e; ++b) {
  ...
  im2col_transpose(in_sub, ...,result); // accumulates with +=
```

`im2col_transpose` writes `out_data[...] += ...` and never clears the buffer, so every batch after the first accumulates on top of its predecessors. With the default build (`nntr_num_threads` is 1 unless `NNTR_NUM_THREADS` is defined) `getNumWorkers()` is 1 and the whole batch runs in one call, so this hits every `batch > 1` forward pass and every `batch > 1` weight-gradient pass. More generally it hits whenever a worker's `[s, e)` range covers more than one batch, i.e. whenever `batch > num_workers`.

Demonstrated with a model of the loop, using the **already fixed** F1 guard so the effect is attributable to the accumulation and not to the guard: a 2-batch `1:2:2` input of all-1s and all-2s with an all-1s 2x2 kernel gives batch 0 `[[1,2,1],[2,4,2],[1,2,1]]` (correct) and batch 1 `[[3,6,3],[6,12,6],[3,6,3]]`, which is `K*(in0+in1)`, where the correct answer is `[[2,4,2],[4,8,4],[2,4,2]]` = `K*in1`.

Scope of the verification, to be precise: this was established by reading the code and by modelling the exact loop structure numerically. It was **not** executed against the compiled layer — the machine this was prepared on has no C++ toolchain, and the layer has no test that would exercise it (see below). A multi-batch unit test is therefore deliberately left out of #4347: it would fail for this reason rather than for anything F1 changes.

Likely fix: zero the buffer per batch, or have `im2col_transpose` clear its output before filling it (it only writes the entries that pass the guards, so the rest must be zero).

---

### Not an audited item — recording a separate `split` finding from the F7 work

Found while fixing item **F7** (PR #4346). This is **not** one of the 83 items in this issue, and it is **not** a memory-safety defect: it is a functional/correctness bug in incremental decode. It is therefore out of scope for this audit and probably deserves its own issue.

**`SplitLayer::incremental_forwarding()` indexes rows relatively, not absolutely.** In `nntrainer/layers/split_layer.cpp`, the axis=3 fast path computes `num_steps = to - from` and then loops `s` over `[0, num_steps)`, addressing `input_.getAddress(b, 0, s, idx * split_w)` and `output_.getAddress(b, 0, s, 0)`. `from` is used only to size the loop, never as an offset. A decode step with `from = N, to = N + 1` therefore copies row `0` rather than row `N`, and the output row written is `0` rather than `N`. **Verification scope, stated honestly:** this is from reading the code only. I did **not** reproduce it — no decode run, no failing test, no instrumented trace. It should be confirmed against an actual `incremental_inference` run before anyone acts on it.

The regression tests added in #4346 deliberately drive `incremental_forwarding()` only with `from == 0`, where the relative and absolute readings coincide, so they do **not** lock in either semantics and will not obstruct whichever fix turns out to be correct.

**Why it does not misbehave today, and when it would.** All six handles come from `ml_tensors_info_create()`, never `ml_tensors_info_create_extended()` — there is no `create_extended` call anywhere in the file. For a non-extended handle, current ml-api reads only the first four entries from the caller ([`ml-api-common.c:561-567`](https://github.com/nnstreamer/api/blob/main/c/src/ml-api-common.c#L561) copies `dimension[0..4)` unconditionally and then stores `is_extended ? dimension[i] : 0` for ranks 4..15), so the extra twelve entries are never touched. The read becomes real if any of these handles is switched to an extended one, or if ml-api goes back to a rank-limit-unaware copy loop — which is exactly what it did between the rank increase and the rank-aware rewrite, the window that makes H4 a real defect rather than a theoretical one.

Fix is the same shape as H4: declare the buffers as `ml_tensor_dimension` and zero-initialize, e.g. `ml_tensor_dimension indim = {28, 28, 1, 1};`.

### 1. `*model` is left dangling non-NULL on failure, and `nn_object()` does not clear `magic` before deleting

[`nn_object()`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/src/nntrainer.cpp#L232-L255) publishes the handle at `:243` *before* the call that can fail, then deletes the object at `:252` and returns the error:

```c
  *model = nnmodel;                      // :243
  …
  status = nntrainer_exception_boundary(f);   // createModel()
  if (status != ML_ERROR_NONE) {
    delete nnmodel;                      // :252  — *model still points here
```

[`ml_train_model_construct_with_conf()`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/src/nntrainer.cpp#L287) has the same shape: on a `loadFromConfig()` failure it calls `ml_train_model_destroy(*model)` and returns without NULLing `*model`.

A caller that reacts to the error by releasing the handle it was given — a reasonable reading of the API, and what any RAII wrapper would do — then calls `ml_train_model_destroy()` on freed memory. `ML_TRAIN_VERIFY_VALID_HANDLE` only rejects NULL, and `ML_TRAIN_GET_VALID_HANDLE` dereferences `obj->magic` ([`nntrainer_internal.h:185-192`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/include/nntrainer_internal.h#L185-L192)) out of the freed block. The two paths differ in severity:

- **`construct_with_conf` / `loadFromConfig` failure** — `ml_train_model_destroy` had already run, and it zeroes the magic (`ML_TRAIN_GET_VALID_HANDLE_LOCKED_RESET` does `obj->magic = 0`, [`:211-219`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/include/nntrainer_internal.h#L211-L219)). A retried destroy is a use-after-free *read* that usually sees 0 and returns `ML_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`.
- **`nn_object` / `createModel` failure** — `delete nnmodel` bypasses `ml_train_model_destroy` entirely, so the magic is **never cleared**. The freed block still reads `ML_NNTRAINER_MAGIC`, the validity check passes, `obj->m.lock()` runs on a freed `std::mutex`, and the model is deleted a second time. Double-free / heap corruption.

Suggested fix: set `*model = NULL` after the destroy in both functions, and in `nn_object()` either publish `*model` only after `createModel()` succeeds, or clear `nnmodel->magic` before `delete`.

### 2. The three tensors-info getters leave `*info` dangling non-NULL on their late failure paths

`ml_train_model_get_input_tensors_info()`, `ml_train_model_get_output_tensors_info()` and `ml_train_model_get_weight()` all follow a successful `ml_tensors_info_create(info)` with error paths that do `ml_tensors_info_destroy(*info); return status;` — for example [`:1232-1236`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/src/nntrainer.cpp#L1232-L1236) — without NULLing `*info`. Same consequence as above for a caller that tries to release what it was handed.

### 3. `ml_train_model_get_weight()` leaks `*info`, and destroys a `*weight` that may never have been written

[`:1441-1444`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/src/nntrainer.cpp#L1441-L1444):

```c
  status = ml_tensors_data_create(*info, weight);
  if (status != ML_ERROR_NONE) {
    ml_tensors_data_destroy(*weight);
    return status;
  }
```

Two problems on one path:

- **`*info` is leaked.** It was created successfully earlier in the function and is not destroyed here, and the function returns an error, so the caller has no handle to release it with. The same omission repeats in the `ml_tensors_data_set_tensor_data` loop at [`:1449-1453`](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/7d14d001c9e70014de515dbd00ee6986d50d365f/api/capi/src/nntrainer.cpp#L1449-L1453).
- **`*weight` is destroyed although `ml_tensors_data_create` may not have written it.** The caller's `ml_tensors_data_h` is an out-param; if the create failed before assigning it, this destroys whatever the caller happened to pass in. A caller that NULL-initialized gets a harmless `ML_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`; a caller that did not gets a destroy on an indeterminate pointer.

Suggested fix: destroy `*info` on both paths and set `*info = NULL`, and do not touch `*weight` unless `ml_tensors_data_create()` succeeded.

None of this is reachable from a passing test, which is why no CI job shows it — there is also no sanitizer configured in this repository, so ASan would not catch the double-free either.
